## White letters: who's who

I'm about halfway through initial transcriptions of the [White letters](https://neelsmith.quarto.pub/personal/familyhistory/whiteletters/), and so far have encountered references to twenty-four different members of the White family spread across three generations. Nicknames, preference for middle or first names and accompanying free variation in the order of names, and generosity in honoring other family members with repeated names can make these difficult to keep straight. James Herbert White appears in census records as "James H." but can be "Bertie" in letters. I have not seen any instance of Candace Myra White's full name: she can be Candace M., Myra C., or just Myra (or Mira).  Hirams, Georges and Henrys all proliferate across many generations of the White family.

I've put together this summary chart to help me or anyone else who dips into the letters. It is (intentionally) *not* a complete family tree: it shows the family relations only of names I have found in the letters, all of which fall between 1842 and 1860. Other family members (whether previously deceased, not yet born or married into the family, or simply not mentioned in the letters) do not appear here.


The links on each name lead to automatically generated pages. These pages list source material I have transcribed (including material outside the White letters) and indexed to the individual, and summarize conclusions about the chronology and family relations of the individual that can be based on the transcribed sources.




### Key

- orange background: recipients of letters
- yellow background: senders of letters
